Device Owner gives maximum uninstall protection, but Android permits it only on a new or reset device with no accounts or work profiles. If Android rejects it, the normal installation will continue.
Install over Wi-Fi from a phone

1. ON THE TARGET DEVICE
Open Settings → About and tap Build number seven times. Then open Developer options → Wireless debugging and enable it. The phone and target must use the same normal Wi-Fi network.

2. PAIR — ONCE ONLY
On the target, tap “Pair device with pairing code” and keep that dialog open. Enter its IP, temporary pairing port, and six digits in this app. Tap Pair.

3. CONNECT
Close the code dialog. On the main Wireless debugging screen find “IP address & port”. This is a different port. Enter it as the connection port and tap Connect.

4. INSTALL
After the app says Connected, tap INSTALL. Device discovery is optional: you can always type the IP and both ports manually.

If Wireless debugging is unavailable, open the separate USB guide.

IMPORTANT: this Parent Installer installs from a phone over Wi-Fi. A normal USB cable between a phone and TV usually cannot work: the TV port is intended for flash drives, not for receiving ADB from a phone.

OPTION 1 — FLASH DRIVE
Download the AndroidScreenTimer APK, copy it to a USB drive, open the file on the target, and allow installation from that source. Then enable screen control manually in Accessibility.

OPTION 2 — COMPUTER
Enable USB debugging on the target, connect it to a computer, approve the RSA key on the target, and run: adb install -r AndroidScreenTimer.apk.

OPTION 3 — LEGACY NETWORK ADB
If the firmware offers ADB over network / Network debugging, enable it and enter the displayed IP and port as the connection endpoint. Port 5555 is common, but use the value shown by the device. Pairing by code is usually unnecessary in this mode.
\n\nScreen control could not be enabled automatically. Open Accessibility on the target device and enable Android Screen Timer manually.

Logging is always on and survives restarts. Important results are shown first: the target IP and port, successful connection, installer response, or exact error. If discovery is still running, wait until its indicator disappears (up to 10 seconds), then tap Refresh log. All addresses, ADB commands, complete responses, and stack traces remain below. Pairing codes, the private ADB key, and APK binary contents are hidden. Copy the log or save it as TXT; old entries rotate automatically.
